title: Control of heart rate and ECGs; Food tests and chromatography
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EX08#t1 term and clue written for the game; EX08#t4 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t4 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BM09a#N.4a, EX08#N.7, BM09a#N.13, EX08#N.10, BM09a#N.14, EX08#N.14a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Myogenic
items.clue: Describes muscle that contracts without any nerve impulse

items.label: Bundle of His
items.clue: Carries the wave of excitation down the septum to the apex

items.label: Reducing sugars
items.clue: Group made up of all monosaccharides plus maltose and lactose

items.label: Biuret test
items.clue: A change from blue to lilac shows that peptide bonds are present

questions.stem: A solution gives a negative result with iodine. With Benedict's reagent, heated, it stays blue. A fresh sample is boiled with dilute hydrochloric acid, neutralised, and tested with Benedict's again: a brick-red precipitate forms. What does the solution contain?

options.text: A reducing sugar, because the final Benedict's test was positive.
Starch, which the acid broke down into glucose.
A non-reducing sugar, such as sucrose, and no reducing sugar.
A reducing sugar made by the acid joining smaller sugars by condensation.

questions.explanation: Negative first, positive after acid hydrolysis: the acid split a non-reducing sugar into reducing monosaccharides.

questions.stem: On an ECG recorded at 25 mm s⁻¹, the distance between two R peaks is 30 mm. What is the heart rate in beats per minute?
questions.explanation: R–R time = 30 ÷ 25 = 1.2 s. Rate = 60 ÷ 1.2 = 50 beats min⁻¹.

questions.stem: 1.0 cm³ of DCPIP is decolourised by 0.50 cm³ of a 1.0 mg cm⁻³ vitamin C solution. The same volume of DCPIP is decolourised by 2.5 cm³ of a fruit drink. What is the vitamin C concentration of the drink?

options.text: 5.0 mg cm⁻³
0.20 mg cm⁻³
1.25 mg cm⁻³
0.50 mg cm⁻³

questions.explanation: The DCPIP needs 0.50 cm³ × 1.0 mg cm⁻³ = 0.50 mg of vitamin C. The drink supplied that in 2.5 cm³: 0.50 ÷ 2.5 = 0.20 mg cm⁻³.

questions.stem: A person stands up quickly and their blood pressure falls for a few seconds. Which sequence describes the feedback response that restores blood pressure?

options.text: Baroreceptors in the arteries send fewer impulses to the medulla, which sends sympathetic impulses that raise heart rate and stroke volume.
Baroreceptors detect the fall and the medulla sends impulses along the vagus nerve to reduce heart rate, because a lower rate lets the pressure recover.
The medulla sends the impulses that cause each heartbeat more frequently, because the heart cannot beat at all unless the medulla drives it.
Baroreceptors in the heart wall detect the fall in pressure and the heart raises its own rate without any involvement of the medulla.

questions.stem: A sample of milk is tested. Heated with Benedict's reagent: an orange-red precipitate. With biuret reagent: lilac. With iodine in potassium iodide: stays orange-brown. Which conclusion is supported?

options.text: It contains glucose and no other sugar.
It contains starch, protein and a reducing sugar.
It contains a reducing sugar and protein, but no detectable lipid.
It contains a reducing sugar and protein, but no detectable starch.

questions.explanation: Precipitate: reducing sugar. Lilac: peptide bonds, so protein. No blue-black: no starch detected.

questions.stem: In a heart transplant, the nerves linking the donor heart to the medulla are cut, and they do not regrow for many months. Which statement about the transplanted heart is correct?

options.text: It cannot beat until the nerves regrow, because each beat needs an impulse from the brain.
It beats steadily, because its SAN starts each beat, but the medulla can no longer adjust its rate quickly.
Its rate still rises at once when blood pressure falls, because the baroreceptors are in the heart wall itself.
Its atria and ventricles now contract together, because nerves from the brain normally time the ventricles.
